SPX.label: S&P 500
SPX.source: Polygon I:SPX 8/28 settled close, -19.23 points, re-derived from our own daily series this run. Two sessions old now and nothing has traded since, which is worth saying plainly on a Sunday: this is Friday's number, not a stale one. The week finished +0.49%, a second consecutive weekly gain, so a hawkish Friday did not undo the week. Internals disagreed with the headline: 1,791 advancers against 2,888 decliners, only 37% of issues higher. NOT ATH - 1.119% below the 8/13/26 record close 7798.99. Up 2.96% over the last month measured against the 7/31 close

NDX.source: Polygon I:NDX 8/28 settled close, -0.70%, our own bars. SOX.label: Philly Semis
SOX.source: Polygon I:SOX 8/28 settled close, -3.47%, still the worst thing on this board by a wide margin. Marvell -10.28% and Nvidia -4.58% did most of it. Dell reports Tuesday and Broadcom Wednesday, so this gets re-tested within 72 hours

DJI.label: Dow 30
DJI.source: Polygon I:DJI 8/28 settled close, -9.45 points, -0.02% - effectively unchanged, and the least AI-exposed of the four benchmarks was the best of them on the day. For the WEEK the Dow added 0.53% and snapped a two-week losing streak. NOT ATH - 1.452% below the 8/5/26 record close 54349.12 (record high 54744.33 the same day)

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Polygon I:VIX 8/28 settled close, -0.55%. Two days on, this is still the most interesting fact on the board: on the day the Fed Chair triggered the largest hawkish repricing of the year, equity volatility FELL. VIX3M settled 17.48, so front-to-three-month is 14.43/17.48 = 0.8255 against 0.8263 Thursday - still steep contango, still complacency. VXN, the Nasdaq-100 volatility index, settled 19.92, -1.58%, its LOWEST CLOSE SINCE 2026-01-12 on our own two-year series, and -9.37% for the week. Nothing over the weekend disturbed that: no Fed speaker, no clarification, no Sunday-show appearance by a Fed or Treasury principal. Whatever the VIX is telling you, it has now had 48 hours to change its mind and has not been given a reason to

US10Y.label: US 10Y
US10Y.source: Friday settle, +4.3bp, re-read from TradingEconomics' country bond-yield page this run at 4.7170/+0.0430 and corroborated on TE /bonds at the same 4.7170. LESSON #166-A HAS CLEARED: yesterday TE's dedicated 10Y page read 4.69/+0.01pp and was contradicted by TE's own overview table and four wires, so we logged it DEGRADED. This run all three TE surfaces AGREE at 4.717, which means yesterday's defect was a lagged intraday snapshot that has since settled, not a persistent vendor fault. No DEGRADED flag on rates today. CNBC's US10Y quote page shows 4.73%/+0.058 timed 5:05 PM EDT, which is the later cash-market cut rather than a disagreement about the level

US2Y.label: US 2Y
US2Y.source: Friday settle, +11.4bp, re-read from TE's dedicated 2Y page this run at 4.3520/+0.1140 - the single largest move on the board in yield terms and where the Warsh speech actually landed. The curve BEAR FLATTENED and we re-derive it rather than carrying it: 4.717 minus 4.352 is 36.5bp of 2s10s, against 4.674 minus 4.238 or 43.6bp the day before, so 7.1bp of flattening. The 5-year settled 4.49% (+8.6bp) and the 30-year 5.21% (+1.1bp), so the whole belly moved and the long end barely did. Attributed rather than asserted: WSJ and Dow Jones called the 2-year's +0.118pp the largest single-day yield gain following a Jackson Hole Chair speech since Greenspan in 1996 - their claim, their basis. Cut probability is still exactly ZERO at every meeting through January 2027

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: October contract SETTLEMENT, -$0.13, -0.16%, on two sources NEW this run rather than carried: Barchart's CLV26 contract page and energynow.ca independently give 83.40 / -0.13 / -0.16%. energynow adds the citable weekly basis we lacked yesterday - down $3.66 or 4.2% from the prior Friday's $87.06 close - and notes TradingView's continuous contract at 83.43 after the close, confirming the settle. The driver has not changed: recovering Hormuz tanker traffic plus Iran-Oman corridor talks reframed Iran as a sanctions story rather than a supply story. That reframing now has a live test, because the Venezuela agreement developed over the weekend in the direction of MORE confusion, not less

BRENT.label: Brent Crude
BRENT.source: October contract SETTLEMENT, -$0.39, -0.43%. NEW DATA DEFECT LOGGED, lesson #167-A: TradingEconomics' Brent page contradicted ITSELF this run. Its data table read 88.290/-0.23/-0.26% while the narrative text on the SAME page read that Brent fell to $89.3 on Friday, extending weekly losses to over 5%. The narrative is right - pflpetroleum's daily report and Forbes both put the settle at 89.31 - and the 88.29 print is a contract-roll artefact, since Brent October expires Aug 31 and quote vendors roll early. We ship 89.31 and name the basis. This is a different failure mode from yesterday's: there a dedicated page lagged a wire, here one page disagrees with its own prose. Brent fell more than 5% on the week, the first weekly loss in three

GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: Polygon C:XAUUSD settled UTC-day bar, -3.04%, its worst session since 2026-02-05 on our own series - and still the cleanest confirmation anywhere that Friday was a real rates event rather than a headline. Note a correction to our own prior print: this run's re-read gives the prior close as 4594.37, not the 4594.29 we shipped yesterday, so the delta is -3.0359% rather than -3.0342%. Independent corroboration on the level from Kitco, which is a candidate primary source we have flagged twice: 4454.40, -$146.20, -3.18% timed 17:00 EST Aug 28. The percentage differs from ours only because Kitco's prior-close cut is not the UTC-day cut. Silver did worse at -4.17% and palladium rose 5.32% on the same day, so this was not uniform metals selling. NOT a record - 19.160% below the 1/28/26 record close 5510.73

BTC.label: Bitcoin
BTC.source: Coinbase public spot at 11:13:38 UTC Sunday - the ONLY live price on this board today - against Polygon's settled 8/29 UTC-day close of 78233.93, both re-derived this run (Polygon crypto live and minute endpoints return 403; entitlement absent, not retried). EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: Polygon C:EURJPY settled 8/28 close, effectively unchanged at -0.01%. That is the point of showing it: on the day the front end of the US curve moved 11bp, the yen carry cross did not move at all. No funding stress, no forced unwind, no risk-parity signature anywhere in FX. NOT a record - 1.020% below the 4/16/26 record close 187.552. The dollar-index gap we flagged yesterday is unchanged: no citable Friday DXY close, only 99.20 at 9:13 ET pre-speech, with the wires putting the dollar +0.4% to +0.53% on the day, which we report as a range rather than a level

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: Polygon C:AUDJPY settled 8/28 close, -0.01%, the second carry cross and the same message: flat. One precise distinction that our ATH check forces and that a careless read would get wrong - AUD/JPY set its highest INTRADAY HIGH of the last two years on Friday at 114.96, but its CLOSE is still 0.115% below the 6/2/26 record close of 114.752. That is a high-water intraday mark, NOT a record close, and it is not reported as one. Both carry crosses sitting still while US front-end yields jumped remains the strongest evidence that Friday was a repricing rather than a stress event
